svg.title: When fine-grained feedback helps, hurts, and changes behavior
svg.desc: Three panels from the paper. (a) Decayed process rewards yield relative score changes from outcome-only GRPO of +10.4% on NS, -2.2% on RC, -2.1% on CS, and +45.4% on the more complex Fine Cut task. (b) Fixed-weight process reward rises while outcome reward declines after update 30. Decaying lambda over updates 20 to 30 mitigates reward hacking; held-out truncation falls from 44.1% to 6.2%. Faint lines connect recorded training observations; thick lines are centered five-observation means. (c) Decayed PRM relative to GRPO increases frames seen 1.54 times, reasoning length 1.67 times, and explicit self-correction markers 1.89 times. These metrics do not verify reasoning quality or correctness of corrections; task complexity and horizon vary together.
